name: Qualitative or Quantitative Defects of Troponin

criteria.description: Presence of cardiomyopathy symptoms such as exercise intolerance and arrhythmias
Abnormal qualitative or quantitative troponin levels detected by immunoassays
Identification of pathogenic variants in troponin genes (TNNI3, TNNT2, or TNNC1)
Echocardiographic or MRI evidence of structural cardiac abnormalities consistent with troponin defects

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical cardiomyopathy symptoms plus abnormal troponin assay results and confirmatory genetic testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, laboratory, and genetic data due to phenotypic variability.

searchTerms: thickened heart muscle running in families
family history of enlarged heart muscle
worsening shortness of breath with activity

common.symptomName: Chest discomfort related to myocardial ischemia
searchTerms: chest pain from reduced blood flow

occasional.symptomName: Exercise intolerance without overt heart failure
searchTerms: poor exercise tolerance without heart failure
difficulty exercising despite normal heart function
exercise intolerance without heart failure signs

rare.symptomName: Sudden cardiac death in young individuals
searchTerms: unexpected sudden death in young people

laboratory: Reduced or absent troponin protein levels on immunoassay
Elevated cardiac biomarkers during episodes of myocardial injury
imaging: Echocardiography showing hypertrophic or restrictive cardiomyopathy
Cardiac MRI demonstrating myocardial fibrosis and abnormal contractility
genetic: Pathogenic variants in TNNI3, TNNT2, or TNNC1 genes
Familial segregation of troponin gene mutations
other: Electrocardiogram abnormalities including arrhythmias and conduction delays
Histopathology showing myocyte disarray and fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Typically caused by sarcomeric protein mutations other than troponin
Absence of qualitative troponin defects on immunoassay
Predominant ventricular dilation with systolic dysfunction

redFlags: Sudden cardiac arrest or unexplained syncope
Family history of sudden cardiac death
Rapid progression of heart failure symptoms
references: Orphanet: Qualitative or Quantitative Defects of Troponin (ORPHA:284786)
Maron BJ, et al. Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Clinical Spectrum and Management. Circulation. 2014.
Watkins H, et al. Genetic basis of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: from mutation identification to clinical management. Lancet. 2011.
